proposal: The Mandate recommends redistributing the Department's offices and programs: career, technical, and adult education to the Department of Labor; postsecondary programs to Labor's Employment and Training Administration, with national-security-related programs to State; Indian education programs to the Bureau of Indian Education; and the statistics office (NCES) to the Census Bureau, with research possibly to the National Science Foundation.
remaining: Codification by Congress: the House committee advanced transfer bills, the Senate committee advanced a bill to block four of the transfers, and neither has reached a floor vote in the sources reviewed.

status_summary: As of 2026-10-08 ED has signed 14 interagency agreements (IAAs) with six agencies. The first, signed on 2025-05-21 according to a Department of Labor release, gives Labor a larger role in day-to-day administration of adult education (WIOA Title II) and Perkins career and technical education programs; ED's release says ED keeps its legal responsibilities, positions, policy authority and oversight. ED's release of 2025-11-18 announced six more agreements: two with Labor (elementary and secondary programs; most Higher Education Act postsecondary grants), one with Interior (Indian education programs), two with HHS (foreign medical school accreditation review; campus child care grants) and one with State (international education and foreign language programs, including Fulbright-Hays), with the Labor and Interior partnerships stated to operate with proper oversight by ED. A February 2026 round moved six K-12 grant programs to HHS and a foreign-gift reporting portal to State (per Education Week), and four agreements announced on 2026-06-16 cover special education and rehabilitation programs with HHS and civil rights enforcement, student privacy and training and advisory services with the Department of Justice; ED's release says that under the civil rights partnership ED keeps all its statutory authorities and functions, and Education Week describes the arrangements as moving special education and civil rights work to the other agencies. Destination agencies largely match the Mandate, but the vehicle is interagency agreements rather than a Reorganization Act, ED states it keeps statutory responsibility, and staff and day-to-day work were only beginning to shift in mid-2026. Statistics and research functions had not been assigned in the sources reviewed.

timeline.event: ED signs its first interagency agreement, with Labor, under which Labor takes a larger role in day-to-day administration of adult education and family literacy (WIOA Title II) and Perkins career and technical education programs alongside ED staff; the Labor release (dated 2025-07-15) gives the signing date, and ED's release says ED retains its legal responsibilities, positions, policy authority and oversight.

ED announces six agreements with four agencies (the ED page shows a last-reviewed date of 2025-11-18 and no printed release date): Labor receives a larger role in elementary and secondary programs and most Higher Education Act postsecondary grants; Interior takes over administration of Indian education programs; HHS assesses foreign medical school accreditation standards and manages campus child care grants; State takes over administration of Fulbright-Hays international education programs. The release says the Labor and Interior partners act with proper oversight by ED, and ED says it will work with Congress to codify the reforms.

ED announces an agreement moving six K-12 grant programs (including Full-Service Community Schools and Promise Neighborhoods) to HHS, and the State Department takes over the portal for foreign gifts to colleges. ED states it keeps statutory responsibility and oversight.

ED announces four new interagency agreements, added to ten earlier ones: one with HHS covering special education and rehabilitative services, and three with the Department of Justice covering civil rights complaint enforcement, student privacy protection, and training and advisory services drawing on DOJ's school desegregation role. ED's release says ED keeps all its statutory authorities and functions under the civil rights partnership and that the HHS agreement does not alter the federal government's duty to enforce disability laws; Education Week describes the effect as special education and rehabilitation programs moving to HHS (Administration on Disabilities) and OCR, student privacy enforcement and four equity assistance centers moving to Justice.
ED's count of interagency agreements reaches 14 across HHS, Justice, State, Labor, Interior, and Treasury.

House Education and Workforce Committee marks up and advances ten bills that would codify the interagency agreements (all except the most recent special education and civil rights transfers), mostly on party lines.
Senate HELP Committee advances S. 5046, 13-9, to bar interagency-agreement transfers of the special education, elementary and secondary, postsecondary, and Indian education offices.
ED begins reassigning some employees to other agencies' buildings in the Washington area (source says the week before 2026-09-15; day approximate).
